children: A fragile and uncertain geopolitical backdrop, with oil prices rising due to renewed hostilities in the Middle East, should sustain demand for the U.S. dollar as a safe-haven asset, Eleonex CEO Stefan Arsenovic says in a note. Persistent tensions in the Middle East also sustain inflation concerns and reinforcing the case for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, he says. The dollar falls on Monday, for now shrugging off higher oil prices in thin trade due to a U.S. public holiday and helped by gains in the Japanese yen. This week's input for the dollar could come from producer prices on Thursday and consumer prices on Friday. The DXY dollar index falls 0.2% to 98.953. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
